items.text: Must have been under State Pension age (66) at the time of the partner's death.

problems.claim: Must have been under State Pension age (66) at the time of the partner's death.
problems.note: The source says under State Pension age but does not give the age as 66.
problems.quote: When your partner died, you must have been: under State Pension age

quotes.quote: When your partner died, you must have been: under State Pension age

items.action: Cite the official State Pension age page for the age of 66 and say it is rising to 67.
items.reason: 66 is right for most deaths today, but State Pension age is rising, so a fixed figure could wrongly include or exclude people near the threshold whose partner dies later.

items.name: Bereavement Support Payment

value.description: Deceased must have paid at least 25 weeks of Class 1 or 2 NI contributions, or died from a work-related accident or disease.

items.text: Deceased must have paid at least 25 weeks of Class 1 or 2 NI contributions, or died from a work-related accident or disease.

problems.claim: Deceased must have paid at least 25 weeks of Class 1 or 2 NI contributions, or died from a work-related accident or disease.
problems.note: The source says 'a certain amount' of contributions and does not give a figure of 25 weeks; the work accident or disease alternative is stated.
problems.quote: paid a certain amount of Class 1 or Class 2 National Insurance contributions in any one tax year since 6 April 1975 died because of an accident at work or a disease caused by work

quotes.quote: paid a certain amount of Class 1 or Class 2 National Insurance contributions in any one tax year since 6 April 1975 died because of an accident at work or a disease caused by work

items.action: Cite the official guidance for the 25-week figure and add that the contributions must be in a single tax year.
items.reason: Without 'in one tax year', people whose partner paid 25 weeks spread over several years with no single qualifying year could be wrongly told they qualify.

items.name: Funeral Expenses Payment

value.description: You or your partner must be receiving Universal Credit, Pension Credit, Income Support, income-based JSA, income-related ESA, Housing Benefit, or the child tax credit and working tax credit element at the maximum rate.

items.text: You or your partner must be receiving Universal Credit, Pension Credit, Income Support, income-based JSA, income-related ESA, Housing Benefit, or the child tax credit and working tax credit element at the maximum rate.

problems.claim: You or your partner must be receiving Universal Credit, Pension Credit, Income Support, income-based JSA, income-related ESA, Housing Benefit, or the child tax credit and working tax credit element at the maximum rate.
problems.note: UC, income-related ESA, Pension Credit and Housing Benefit are listed, but Income Support, income-based JSA and tax credits are not in the text.
problems.quote: You (or your partner) must get one or more of the following: Universal Credit income-related Employment and Support Allowance Pension Credit Housing Benefit

quotes.quote: You (or your partner) must get one or more of the following: Universal Credit income-related Employment and Support Allowance Pension Credit Housing Benefit

items.action: Replace the list with the qualifying benefits exactly as the official page gives them, and remove the garbled tax credit wording.
items.reason: People on Income Support, income-based JSA or tax credits could be wrongly told they qualify. The tax credit condition as written is not a real rule.

items.name: Funeral Expenses Payment

value.description: You are responsible for the funeral costs of a partner, close relative, or close friend where there is no other close relative able to pay.

items.text: You are responsible for the funeral costs of a partner, close relative, or close friend where there is no other close relative able to pay.

problems.claim: You are responsible for the funeral costs of a partner, close relative, or close friend where there is no other close relative able to pay.
problems.note: The text covers partners and close relatives or friends, but its conditions are about the deceased having no partner or the partner being unable to claim, and a close relative who is working or not on a qualifying benefit may stop you getting the payment. It does not say 'no other close relative able to pay'.
problems.quote: If you’re a close relative or friend You might be able to get a Funeral Expenses Payment if: the deceased did not have a partner when they died the partner of the deceased or parent of a deceased child cannot claim

quotes.quote: If you’re a close relative or friend You might be able to get a Funeral Expenses Payment if: the deceased did not have a partner when they died the partner of the deceased or parent of a deceased child cannot claim

items.action: Reword the rule to match the official conditions about the deceased's partner and close relatives who work or aren't on a qualifying benefit.
items.reason: Claimants whose case depends on the partner rule, or on another relative's work or benefit status, could be judged eligible or ineligible wrongly because 'able to pay' isn't the real test.

items.name: Tell Us Once

value.description: Death registered in England, Scotland or most of Wales (not available in all areas).

items.text: Death registered in England, Scotland or most of Wales (not available in all areas).

problems.claim: Death registered in England, Scotland or most of Wales (not available in all areas).
problems.note: The text ties eligibility to where the person lived (England, Scotland or Wales) and to the death being registered or reported to a coroner; it does not say 'most of Wales' or that some areas are excluded.
problems.quote: You can use Tell Us Once if the person who died was living in England, Scotland or Wales.

quotes.quote: You can use Tell Us Once if the person who died was living in England, Scotland or Wales.

items.action: Say the service covers people who lived in England, Scotland or Wales, and remove 'most of Wales' and the claim that some areas are excluded.
items.reason: Families of people who lived in Wales could wrongly be told they may not qualify, and tying eligibility to where the death was registered rather than where the person lived could mislead some users.

items.name: Register the death

value.description: A person has died in England or Wales.

items.text: A person has died in England or Wales.

problems.claim: A person has died in England or Wales.
problems.note: The page covers deaths in the UK or abroad but never limits the service to deaths in England or Wales, so that restriction is not in the text.
problems.quote: Find out how to register a death in the UK or abroad.

quotes.quote: Find out how to register a death in the UK or abroad.

items.action: Cite the page that limits this route to England and Wales, and add the routes for deaths abroad, in Scotland and in Northern Ireland.
items.reason: Most people registering a death in England or Wales are unaffected, but anyone dealing with a death abroad or in Scotland or Northern Ireland could be wrongly told the service doesn't apply to them or not sent to the right route.

items.name: Apply for probate

value.description: Person has died leaving assets held in their sole name.

items.text: Person has died leaving assets held in their sole name.

problems.claim: Person has died leaving assets held in their sole name.
problems.note: The text refers to a person who has died and suggests jointly owned assets may not need probate, but it never mentions 'sole name' or makes this a stated condition.
problems.quote: You may not need probate if the person who died: only had savings owned shares or money with others

quotes.quote: You may not need probate if the person who died: only had savings owned shares or money with others

items.action: Cite an official page that links probate to assets in the person's sole name, or reword the condition to match the source.
items.reason: Making 'sole name' a strict condition could wrongly screen out people who need probate for jointly held assets, such as property owned as tenants in common.

items.name: National Insurance number

value.description: UK citizens are automatically assigned one — applies mainly to non-UK nationals who have arrived to work or study.

items.text: UK citizens are automatically assigned one — applies mainly to non-UK nationals who have arrived to work or study.

problems.claim: UK citizens are automatically assigned one — applies mainly to non-UK nationals who have arrived to work or study.
problems.note: Automatic issue is only described for UK residents where a Child Benefit claim was made, not for all UK citizens, and the text never says the service is mainly for non-UK nationals arriving to work or study.
problems.quote: You’ll normally be sent a National Insurance number in the 3 months before your 16th birthday if both the following are true: you live in the UK a parent or guardian has filled in a Child Benefit claim form for you

quotes.quote: You’ll normally be sent a National Insurance number in the 3 months before your 16th birthday if both the following are true: you live in the UK a parent or guardian has filled in a Child Benefit claim form for you

items.action: Limit automatic issue to UK residents with a Child Benefit claim and remove the 'mainly non-UK nationals' claim.
items.reason: UK citizens with no Child Benefit claim made for them could be wrongly told they already have a number and don't need to apply.

items.name: British citizenship (naturalisation)

value.description: Must be of good character (no serious criminal record) and demonstrate knowledge of English, Welsh or Scottish Gaelic.

items.text: Must be of good character (no serious criminal record) and demonstrate knowledge of English, Welsh or Scottish Gaelic.

problems.claim: Must be of good character (no serious criminal record) and demonstrate knowledge of English, Welsh or Scottish Gaelic.
problems.note: The source states good character and the language requirement, but it does not define good character as having no serious criminal record.
problems.quote: prove your knowledge of English , Welsh or Scottish Gaelic have passed the life in the UK test intend to continue living in the UK be of good character

quotes.quote: prove your knowledge of English , Welsh or Scottish Gaelic have passed the life in the UK test intend to continue living in the UK be of good character

items.action: Remove the 'no serious criminal record' definition, or replace it with the official good character guidance, which also covers immigration breaches, tax affairs and deception.
items.reason: People with minor convictions, immigration breaches or unpaid tax could be wrongly told they meet the good character requirement, and people with some old convictions could be wrongly put off.

items.name: Citizenship ceremony

value.description: Adults aged 18 and over must attend in person. Children under 18 can be included on a parent's ceremony.

items.text: Adults aged 18 and over must attend in person. Children under 18 can be included on a parent's ceremony.

problems.claim: Adults aged 18 and over must attend in person. Children under 18 can be included on a parent's ceremony.
problems.note: The text says people aged 18 or over must attend, but it never says 'in person' and says nothing about adding children under 18 to a parent's ceremony.
problems.quote: You need to attend a citizenship ceremony if you’re 18 or over and have successfully applied to become a British citizen.

quotes.quote: You need to attend a citizenship ceremony if you’re 18 or over and have successfully applied to become a British citizen.

items.action: Cite the ceremony guidance for in-person attendance and for how children under 18 are treated, or remove the claim about children.
items.reason: Parents could be misled about whether their children under 18 must attend or are covered by the parent's ceremony. Adults are correctly told they must attend.

items.name: View or prove your immigration status

value.description: Must have a UKVI account with an eVisa or EU Settlement Scheme status.

items.text: Must have a UKVI account with an eVisa or EU Settlement Scheme status.

problems.claim: Must have a UKVI account with an eVisa or EU Settlement Scheme status.
problems.note: The text says you need a UKVI account and an eVisa, but it never mentions EU Settlement Scheme status as another qualifying route.
problems.quote: You’ll need the details you use to sign in to your UKVI account.

quotes.quote: You’ll need the details you use to sign in to your UKVI account.

items.action: Cite the official guidance saying EU Settlement Scheme status can be viewed and proved through a UKVI account.
items.reason: EU Settlement Scheme status holders are told they qualify under a separate route, and only that group would be misled if the route were wrong.

items.name: Visa / leave to enter

value.description: Non-UK, non-Irish national wishing to enter the UK (some nationalities require visa; others may enter visa-free for short stays).

items.text: Non-UK, non-Irish national wishing to enter the UK (some nationalities require visa; others may enter visa-free for short stays).

problems.claim: Non-UK, non-Irish national wishing to enter the UK (some nationalities require visa; others may enter visa-free for short stays).
problems.note: The text covers people who are not British or Irish and says they may need a visa or an ETA, but it never says outright that some nationalities can enter visa-free for short stays.
problems.quote: Check if you need a UK Visa, electronic travel authorisation (ETA) or get access to an eVisa to prove your immigration status if you’re not a British citizen or Irish national

quotes.quote: Check if you need a UK Visa, electronic travel authorisation (ETA) or get access to an eVisa to prove your immigration status if you’re not a British citizen or Irish national

items.action: Cite the check-if-you-need-a-visa guidance for visa-free short stays and mention the ETA requirement.
items.reason: Visa-free short stays are real, but leaving out the ETA could mislead visa-free visitors who still need permission to travel.

items.name: Electoral roll update

value.description: Must be 16 or over to register (18 to vote in most elections).

items.text: Must be 16 or over to register (18 to vote in most elections).

problems.claim: Must be 16 or over to register (18 to vote in most elections).
problems.note: The minimum age of 16 applies only in England and Northern Ireland (it is 14 in Scotland and Wales), and the text gives 18 only for particular elections, such as general elections, not as a rule for most elections.
problems.quote: If you live in England or Northern Ireland You must be aged 16 or over to register.

quotes.quote: If you live in England or Northern Ireland You must be aged 16 or over to register.

items.action: State that the minimum age to register is 16 in England and Northern Ireland and 14 in Scotland and Wales, and limit the age-18 rule to elections such as general elections.
items.reason: Young people in Scotland and Wales would be wrongly told they are too young to register, and 16 and 17-year-olds there would be wrongly told they can't vote in most elections.

items.name: Electoral roll update

value.description: British, Irish, or qualifying Commonwealth citizen (EU citizens can vote in local elections).

items.text: British, Irish, or qualifying Commonwealth citizen (EU citizens can vote in local elections).

problems.claim: British, Irish, or qualifying Commonwealth citizen (EU citizens can vote in local elections).
problems.note: The text supports British, Irish and Commonwealth citizens (Commonwealth only with permission to enter or stay), but in England and Northern Ireland only certain EU citizens can vote in local elections: those from named countries, or those with continuous permission since 31 December 2020.
problems.quote: You can register to vote if you're a British citizen or an Irish citizen. You can also register if you have permission (or do not need permission) to enter or stay in the UK, Channel Islands or Isle of Man and you're: a Commonwealth citizen

quotes.quote: You can register to vote if you're a British citizen or an Irish citizen. You can also register if you have permission (or do not need permission) to enter or stay in the UK, Channel Islands or Isle of Man and you're: a Commonwealth citizen

items.action: Say Commonwealth citizens need permission to enter or stay, and that in England and Northern Ireland only certain EU citizens can vote in local elections.
items.reason: Some EU citizens in England and Northern Ireland would be wrongly told they can vote in local elections, and Commonwealth citizens without permission to stay could wrongly think they qualify.

items.name: Voter Authority Certificate

value.description: Must be eligible to vote (registered on the electoral roll as a British, Irish, or qualifying Commonwealth citizen).

items.text: Must be eligible to vote (registered on the electoral roll as a British, Irish, or qualifying Commonwealth citizen).

problems.claim: Must be eligible to vote (registered on the electoral roll as a British, Irish, or qualifying Commonwealth citizen).
problems.note: Registration is required, but the text never ties this service to the listed nationalities (and the register page lets other nationalities register too).
problems.quote: You must be registered to vote to apply.

quotes.quote: You must be registered to vote to apply.

items.action: Replace the nationality list with the requirement to be registered to vote.
items.reason: Registered voters of other nationalities, such as eligible EU or foreign nationals in some elections, could wrongly be told they cannot apply.

items.name: Voter Authority Certificate

value.description: Must be registered to vote. Only needed if you do not already have an accepted form of photo ID.

items.text: Must be registered to vote. Only needed if you do not already have an accepted form of photo ID.

problems.claim: Must be registered to vote. Only needed if you do not already have an accepted form of photo ID.
problems.note: Registration is required, but the text gives other reasons to apply as well (you no longer look like your photo, or your name is different), and it applies only to voting in person.
problems.quote: You only need to apply for a Voter Authority Certificate if you vote in person and: you do not have accepted photo ID you no longer look like the photo on your ID the name on your photo ID is different

quotes.quote: You only need to apply for a Voter Authority Certificate if you vote in person and: you do not have accepted photo ID you no longer look like the photo on your ID the name on your photo ID is different

items.action: Add that you can also apply if you no longer look like your photo ID or your name has changed, and say the certificate is only for voting in person.
items.reason: People whose photo ID no longer looks like them, or shows an old name, could be told they don't need a certificate and then be turned away at the polling station.

items.name: Right to work check

value.description: Required for all new employees before they begin work. Employer faces civil penalty if not done.

items.text: Required for all new employees before they begin work. Employer faces civil penalty if not done.

problems.claim: Required for all new employees before they begin work. Employer faces civil penalty if not done.
problems.note: The check before employment is stated, but the penalty only applies if the employer also employs an illegal worker, not simply for failing to do the check.
problems.quote: You could face a civil penalty if you employ an illegal worker and have not carried out a correct right to work check.

quotes.quote: You could face a civil penalty if you employ an illegal worker and have not carried out a correct right to work check.

items.action: Reword to say the civil penalty applies when an illegal worker is employed, and that doing the check gives the employer a defence.
items.reason: Employers are told they get a penalty just for skipping the check, but the penalty only applies if they also employ someone without the right to work. This misstates the legal risk for some employers.

items.name: Right to work check

value.description: Non-UK/Irish nationals provide a share code via the UK Visas & Immigration online portal. British/Irish citizens present their passport.

items.text: Non-UK/Irish nationals provide a share code via the UK Visas & Immigration online portal. British/Irish citizens present their passport.

problems.claim: Non-UK/Irish nationals provide a share code via the UK Visas & Immigration online portal. British/Irish citizens present their passport.
problems.note: Checking British/Irish passports and using share codes are both stated, but the text never says the online service is run by UK Visas and Immigration, and the share code is only one option.
problems.quote: British and Irish citizens cannot get an online share code to prove their right to work. You’ll need to check their original documents - for example, their passport or passport card - or use an identity service provider instead.

quotes.quote: British and Irish citizens cannot get an online share code to prove their right to work. You’ll need to check their original documents - for example, their passport or passport card - or use an identity service provider instead.

items.action: Say the share code is one option, and list the other document or Employer Checking Service routes for non-UK/Irish nationals.
items.reason: Non-UK/Irish workers who cannot get a share code are wrongly told it is the only way to prove their right to work, so they and their employers may not find the right route.

items.name: Student Finance (tuition fee + maintenance loans)

value.description: Must be normally resident in England for 3+ years before the course starts, and a UK national or settled person.

items.text: Must be normally resident in England for 3+ years before the course starts, and a UK national or settled person.

problems.claim: Must be normally resident in England for 3+ years before the course starts, and a UK national or settled person.
problems.note: The source requires your home to be in England and 3 years' residence in the UK, Channel Islands or Isle of Man, not 3 years in England specifically; it also includes Irish citizens.
problems.quote: your home is in England you’ve been continuously living in the UK, Channel Islands or Isle of Man for 3 years before the first day of your first academic year

quotes.quote: your home is in England you’ve been continuously living in the UK, Channel Islands or Isle of Man for 3 years before the first day of your first academic year

items.action: Change it to home in England plus 3 years' residence in the UK, Channel Islands or Isle of Man, and add Irish citizens.
items.reason: People who spent part of the 3 years elsewhere in the UK, and Irish citizens, could be wrongly told they don't qualify.

items.name: File annual accounts at Companies House

value.description: Filed for a UK company by an officer, or by anyone with the company's authentication code such as an accountant. Limited liability partnerships can file only certain package accounts.

items.text: Filed for a UK company by an officer, or by anyone with the company's authentication code such as an accountant. Limited liability partnerships can file only certain package accounts.

problems.claim: Filed for a UK company by an officer, or by anyone with the company's authentication code such as an accountant. Limited liability partnerships can file only certain package accounts.
problems.note: The LLP restriction is stated, and the text says a password and authentication code are needed, but it never says the accounts can be filed by an officer or by anyone holding the authentication code, such as an accountant.
problems.quote: Limited liability partnerships can only file certain package accounts using this service.

quotes.quote: Limited liability partnerships can only file certain package accounts using this service.

items.action: Cite the Companies House guidance saying an officer or anyone with the authentication code, such as an accountant, can file.
items.reason: This tells directors and accountants who is allowed to file, which affects how they apply, but it is probably accurate and just needs a source.

items.name: Appeal to Tax Tribunal

value.description: Must have an HMRC decision to appeal. Indirect tax decisions can usually go straight to the tribunal; direct tax decisions must usually be appealed to HMRC first.

items.text: Must have an HMRC decision to appeal. Indirect tax decisions can usually go straight to the tribunal; direct tax decisions must usually be appealed to HMRC first.

problems.claim: Must have an HMRC decision to appeal. Indirect tax decisions can usually go straight to the tribunal; direct tax decisions must usually be appealed to HMRC first.
problems.note: The direct/indirect routing is stated (the text says direct tax 'must' go to HMRC first, with no 'usually'), but the text does not require an HMRC decision: it also allows appeals against decisions by Border Force, the NCA, the WRA and the Gambling Commission.
problems.quote: You must appeal direct tax decisions to HMRC before you can appeal to the tribunal. You can usually appeal indirect tax decisions straight to the tribunal.

quotes.quote: You must appeal direct tax decisions to HMRC before you can appeal to the tribunal. You can usually appeal indirect tax decisions straight to the tribunal.

items.action: Add appeals against Border Force, NCA, WRA and Gambling Commission decisions, and say direct tax appeals must go to HMRC first.
items.reason: People with decisions from these other bodies would wrongly be told they don't qualify, and 'usually' makes the required HMRC-first step for direct tax sound optional.

items.name: Making Tax Digital enrolment

value.description: Mandatory for all VAT-registered businesses. Phased in for income tax self-assessment from 2026.

items.text: Mandatory for all VAT-registered businesses. Phased in for income tax self-assessment from 2026.

problems.claim: Mandatory for all VAT-registered businesses. Phased in for income tax self-assessment from 2026.
problems.note: The VAT part is supported, apart from exemptions; the income tax self-assessment rollout from 2026 is not stated.
problems.quote: All VAT registered businesses should now be signed up for Making Tax Digital for VAT.

quotes.quote: All VAT registered businesses should now be signed up for Making Tax Digital for VAT.

items.action: Add the VAT exemptions and cite the MTD for Income Tax guidance for the 2026 phase-in.
items.reason: Businesses that qualify for an exemption would wrongly be told MTD is mandatory for them, and the income tax phase-in claim has no source.

items.name: Short-term let licence (Scotland)

value.description: Must own or manage a residential property being let for short-term stays.

items.text: Must own or manage a residential property being let for short-term stays.

problems.claim: Must own or manage a residential property being let for short-term stays.
problems.note: The text links the licence to letting out accommodation to temporary guests, but it never says you must own or manage the property or that the property must be residential.
problems.quote: You may need a short-term let licence if you’re letting out accommodation to guests who stay temporarily.

quotes.quote: You may need a short-term let licence if you’re letting out accommodation to guests who stay temporarily.

items.action: Reword to cover anyone providing accommodation to guests on a short-term basis, not just owners or managers of residential property.
items.reason: The 'residential' and 'own or manage' conditions aren't in the sources and could wrongly tell some hosts, such as those letting non-residential or unusual accommodation, that they don't need a licence.

items.name: Street trading licence

value.description: Selling goods or services from a street or public place in England and Wales.

items.text: Selling goods or services from a street or public place in England and Wales.

problems.claim: Selling goods or services from a street or public place in England and Wales.
problems.note: The text covers trading in the street in England and Wales, but it never mentions a 'public place' or says 'goods or services'.
problems.quote: You may need to get a licence to trade in the street in England and Wales

quotes.quote: You may need to get a licence to trade in the street in England and Wales

items.action: Cite the street trading legislation or council guidance that defines 'street' to include public places and covers goods or services.
items.reason: Traders in areas that are open to the public but are not streets, or who sell services, may be told a criterion applies to them based on wording the checked page does not state.

items.name: DBS check

value.description: Role involves working with children or vulnerable adults, or is otherwise in a specified list of eligible positions (healthcare, legal, financial services roles).

items.text: Role involves working with children or vulnerable adults, or is otherwise in a specified list of eligible positions (healthcare, legal, financial services roles).

problems.note: The text mentions children, healthcare and specified positions, but does not mention legal or financial services roles.
problems.quote: An exempted question applies when the individual will be working in specific occupations, for certain licenses or specified positions.

quotes.quote: An exempted question applies when the individual will be working in specific occupations, for certain licenses or specified positions.

items.action: Cite the official DBS eligibility guidance for legal and financial services roles.
items.reason: People in legal or financial roles could be told wrongly whether they qualify for a more detailed check. These roles are probably eligible, but the checked pages don't say so.

items.name: Check and challenge business rates

value.description: Must occupy or own a non-domestic property assessed for business rates in England.

items.text: Must occupy or own a non-domestic property assessed for business rates in England.

problems.claim: Must occupy or own a non-domestic property assessed for business rates in England.
problems.note: The text covers properties in England or Wales that have a rateable value for business rates and refers to 'your property', but it never says you must occupy or own the property, and it never limits the service to England or to non-domestic property.
problems.quote: If you want to report a change to your property or challenge its rateable value, use your business rates valuation account .

quotes.quote: If you want to report a change to your property or challenge its rateable value, use your business rates valuation account .

items.action: Add Wales and remove the unsourced requirement to occupy or own the property.
items.reason: People with property in Wales would wrongly be told they do not qualify, and anyone acting for a property they don't occupy or own could be turned away.

items.name: Get a rod fishing licence

value.description: One licence covers England and Wales, including all of the Border Esk. Scotland and Northern Ireland have separate arrangements.

items.text: One licence covers England and Wales, including all of the Border Esk. Scotland and Northern Ireland have separate arrangements.

problems.claim: One licence covers England and Wales, including all of the Border Esk. Scotland and Northern Ireland have separate arrangements.
problems.note: The text says a single England and Wales licence is needed, but it excludes the River Tweed, and the claim leaves that exception out.
problems.quote: You must have a rod fishing licence for England and Wales if you’re fishing for salmon, trout, freshwater fish, smelt or eel with a rod and line in: England (except the River Tweed) Wales

quotes.quote: you need to buy a rod fishing licence for England and Wales to fish any part of it. This includes the parts of the river and its tributaries that are in Scotland.
There are different rules for fishing in the rest of Scotland and Northern Ireland
You must have a rod fishing licence for England and Wales if you’re fishing for salmon, trout, freshwater fish, smelt or eel with a rod and line in: England (except the River Tweed) Wales

items.action: Add the River Tweed exception to the England and Wales licence rule.
items.reason: People fishing the River Tweed would get the wrong answer about whether this licence applies there, though most anglers are not affected.

items.name: Stamp Duty Land Tax return

value.description: Any purchase of land or property in England (or Northern Ireland) — thresholds vary for first-time buyers, additional properties, etc.

items.text: Any purchase of land or property in England (or Northern Ireland) — thresholds vary for first-time buyers, additional properties, etc.

problems.claim: Any purchase of land or property in England (or Northern Ireland) — thresholds vary for first-time buyers, additional properties, etc.
problems.note: The text confirms England and Northern Ireland and a different threshold for first-time buyers, but for additional properties it describes a 5% higher rate rather than a different threshold, and it lists exemptions (for example freeholds under £40,000) where neither tax nor a return is needed, so not every purchase is covered.
problems.quote: SDLT starts to apply when you buy property that costs: £125,000 for residential properties £300,000 for first-time buyers buying a residential property worth £500,000 or less

quotes.quote: SDLT starts to apply when you buy property that costs: £125,000 for residential properties £300,000 for first-time buyers buying a residential property worth £500,000 or less

items.action: Change 'any purchase' to name the exemptions and describe additional properties as a 5% higher rate, not a different threshold.
items.reason: People buying additional properties could misunderstand how their tax is worked out, and exempt buyers would wrongly think the purchase is covered.

items.name: Land Registry registration (AP1)

value.description: Any purchase of land or property in England or Wales. Also required for remortgages, transfers of equity, and first-time registrations of unregistered land.

items.text: Any purchase of land or property in England or Wales. Also required for remortgages, transfers of equity, and first-time registrations of unregistered land.

problems.claim: Any purchase of land or property in England or Wales. Also required for remortgages, transfers of equity, and first-time registrations of unregistered land.
problems.note: The text covers buying, mortgaging, adding a joint owner and first registration, but 'any purchase' leaves out the short-lease exemption.
